title: compat-layer: strict mime-context routing, payload hysteresis, and per-tool throttles for multipart uploads
author: Aisha Patel
description: Background & motivation: Over the last quarter we've seen a set of recurring issues in the OpenAI-compatibility surface when callers attach files or invoke tool/function calls with multipart/form-data payloads. Problems include: ambiguous or missing Content-Type headers causing incorrect handler routing, large attachments triggering unexpected memory pressure in the serving runtime during batching, and edge cases where chunked uploads are reassembled in ways that break tool-level parsing (e.g., JSON-in-attachment or newline-delimited tool payloads). This PR implements three coordinated defenses in the compat layer and serving runtime to improve safety and predictability for file/tool inputs while preserving backward compatibility for common OpenAI-style clients. Summary of changes and design: 1) Strict mime-context routing: the compat middleware now enforces route-level mime expectations. For public OpenAI compat endpoints we require an explicit Content-Type that maps to one of: multipart/form-data; application/json (for non-file payloads); or application/octet-stream (when signed by a client token permitting raw blobs). If Content-Type is missing or ambiguous we run a conservative content-sniff step limited to the first 512 bytes and only for Content-Type discovery, never as a fallback to change handler semantics. 2) Payload hysteresis thresholds: introduce soft/strict size thresholds per route and per-tool. Soft threshold generates structured warnings (x-compat-warning headers and telemetry) and suggests chunk-aligning; strict threshold rejects the request with 413 and a JSON payload describing recommended chunk size/token limits. Thresholds are configurable via compat config and default to conservative values that avoid common OOMs in continuous-batching. 3) Chunk-aligning and token-aware chunk policy: the client-facing middleware can suggest chunk boundaries aligned to token approximations for text-based attachments (json, ndjson, text/*) to help the runtime avoid mid-token splits that defeat KV-cache reuse and downstream tool parsers. The server also performs an optional reassembly that preserves original boundaries in metadata when trusted (private deployments), and otherwise enforces canonical chunking. 4) Per-tool payload throttling/backpressure: runtime scheduler gets a new light-weight quota for tool attachments expressed as token-equivalents and concurrent-attachment slots. When a high-throughput route would exceed configured attachment throughput we return 429 with Retry-After or enqueue with a short backoff, preventing head-of-line blocking for low-latency generation requests. 5) Compatibility behaviors: existing OpenAI-compat clients continue to work for the common cases; the compat middleware will emit compatibility warnings rather than hard errors for inputs that are within soft thresholds. We only reject at the strict threshold. Implementation notes: - New middleware: packages/compat/middleware/mime_router.go and mime_sniffer.go implement the routing/prioritization. - Runtime changes: runtime/scheduler/payload_throttle.go and runtime/batcher/chunk_align.go implement per-tool quotas and chunk-alignment heuristics. - Config: config/compat.yaml adds route-level soft/strict size thresholds and token-equiv heuristics. - Telemetry: observability/metrics/compat_metrics.go adds histograms and labels for: compat.mime.routed, compat.payload.rejected, compat.payload.warned, compat.attachment.throttled. - Docs & examples: docs/api/compatibility.md updated with the new header semantics and examples for JS/Python clients to perform chunk-aligning. - Tests: tests/integration/compat_uploads.test.ts (end-to-end), tests/unit/mime_router.test.go (unit), plus stress test harness changes under benchmark-lab/upload-stress to validate backpressure. Rollout plan: defaults are conservative and gated behind a feature flag compat.strict_mime_routing. We will flip the flag for hosted beta after an internal canary (perf-canary/compat-upload) validates no regressions on tail-latency and memory. Checklist: - [x] Middleware and runtime implementations - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Telemetry and dashboards (initial metrics) - [x] Docs for client chunking recommendations - [x] Config knobs and feature flag - [x] Backwards-compat smoke runs in perf-canary Known limitations and rationale: - Content-sniffing is limited and gated because blind sniffing can be surprising to clients; we only use it when Content-Type is absent and when it doesn't change handler semantics. - Token-estimate chunk alignment uses a heuristic (byte-to-token mapping) and is advisory for clients. Exact tokenization alignment requires client cooperation. - Some third-party clients that rely on missing Content-Type behavior may get warnings; the rollout will include a grace period. Security considerations: stricter Content-Type enforcement reduces attack surface (ambiguous multipart parsing) and prevents certain content smuggling patterns. Rejecting oversized attachments at the compat layer avoids downstream runtime memory exhaustion. Backwards compatibility: soft thresholds and warnings ensure existing clients continue to work while surface-area for breaking changes is minimized. See release_notes and merge details for timeline and opt-in instructions.
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial mime-router and sniffer middleware; add payload throttle and chunk aligner; wire metrics and config; integration tests and client examples; stress-test harness and perf fixes; docs and changelog updates.
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Left a few nit comments on mime_router.go; asked for clearer separation between sniffing and routing. Requested an explicit limit on sniff bytes (512).

Sofia Nguyen: Concern about thresholds — asked for telemetry labels and suggested adding a percent-based tail metric for attachments to tune soft/strict defaults. Requested an e2e stress run in perf-canary before merging.
Matt Li: Approved with comments — asked to log attachment hashes (non-sensitive) for dedup heuristics and to add a defensive panic recovery in payload_throttle.go.

Aisha Patel (author): Addressed sniffing limit, added compat.mime.sniff_bytes config, wired histograms for percentiles, and added recovery path. Re-ran stress tests and uploaded canary results to Linear ENG-3482.
SRE bot: Noted CI flaky test test-upload-concurrency was re-run twice; final run passed.
merge_details: Merged by Diego Ramos on 2026-03-05 via squash-merge. Squash commit message: 'compat: strict mime routing + payload throttles; add chunk alignment and config knobs (ENG-3482)'. Feature gated behind compat.strict_mime_routing; rollout to hosted beta after perf-canary success. Backported small config stubs to release/2026-02 branch.
release_notes: Added stricter Content-Type enforcement and configurable soft/strict attachment size thresholds for compat endpoints. Clients may receive compat-warning headers if sending ambiguous or large attachments; see docs/api/compatibility.md for recommended chunking examples and feature flag opt-in.
